prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop homepage direction comp for Mouse28, showing a 16:10 first viewport plus enough of the second fold to prove the visual system.
Primary request: Design “Park-Day Dispatch,” a calm trip-planning editorial folio where every blog story feels like a useful piece of a calmer park day. The blog must be unmistakably primary. Make this look like a finished, art-directed website comp, not a wireframe, dashboard, or generic template.
Input images: Image 1 is the authentic family hero photograph and must remain recognizable, undistorted, and dominant. Image 2 is the existing Mouse28 logo and must be preserved exactly as the small header brand mark, without redesigning it. Images 3, 4, and 5 are real painted blog covers; preserve them faithfully and present them as collectible printed objects in the editorial folio.
Composition/framing: 1600-by-1000 landscape desktop canvas. Use an offset editorial spread on a deep navy cloth-like ground. Create a slim, quiet header across the top with the existing logo at left, simple text navigation toward the right, and a cream “Read the Blog” control. Below, make a decisive asymmetrical hero: a large authentic family photograph occupying roughly the right 55 percent, cropped boldly like a clipped travel photograph; on the left, a large cream editorial sheet with the headline “Disney Parks Through Different Eyes”, a brief understated line of body copy that remains visually secondary, and a strong gold “Read the Blog” action. Let a featured-story sheet rise upward from the lower edge into the first viewport like the next page in a planning folio, overlapping the hero composition with the real painted cover for “Welcome to Mouse28” and its title clearly readable. Continue enough below the fold to show “Latest Stories” and two offset route-card objects using the other real painted covers, with small “Guides” and “Podcast” wayfinding visible as supporting destinations. Avoid a generic three-card grid: use staggered paper slips, tabs, route lines, page edges, and editorial sequencing.
Visual world: refined trip-planning folio, editorial magazine spread, calm accessibility-first hierarchy, navy book cloth, warm cream paper, subtle route-rule lines, gold foil details used sparingly, purple ink accents, square-to-soft paper corners, restrained shadows, generous breathing room. Painted covers should look like collectible art prints tucked into the folio, not commodity cards.
Color palette: deep navy #1a1040, cream #fef9ef, gold #d4a843, purple #5b3e9e, with light navy #2d1b69 only where needed.
Typography: high-contrast elegant editorial serif for large headings, clean readable geometric sans serif for navigation and body copy. Calm, large, high-contrast, accessibility-first. No tiny dense text.
Text (verbatim): “Mouse28”; “Disney Parks Through Different Eyes”; “Read the Blog”; “Welcome to Mouse28”; “Latest Stories”; “Guides”; “Podcast”.
Constraints: Show all required verbatim text spelled correctly. Preserve the supplied logo as the only brand mark. Keep the supplied family photo authentic and central. Keep all three supplied article artworks recognizable. Blog hierarchy first, guides and podcast clearly secondary. First-time visitors must immediately understand that this is a practical Disney parks family blog and know to read the blog.
Avoid: Disney characters, any newly invented Mickey ears, any newly invented recognizable castle, additional wordmarks, invented claims, fake statistics, testimonials, em dashes, generic three-card grid, excessive badges, dashboard chrome, glassmorphism, pill overload, loud gradients, sensory clutter, illegible text, mobile mockup frames, watermarks.
